intro: Angola was a Portuguese colony for centuries and endured a long civil war before peace came in 2002.

chapters.title: Kongo and Ndongo
text: The Kingdom of Kongo ruled the north, and the Ndongo kingdom gave Angola its name, from the title ngola. Queen Nzinga resisted the Portuguese for decades in the 1600s.

highlight.title: Queen Nzinga
highlight.text: A brilliant diplomat and war leader, now a national heroine.

chapters.title: Portuguese Angola
text: Portugal founded Luanda in 1576. Millions of enslaved Angolans were shipped to Brazil. In 1961 liberation movements began fighting Portuguese rule.

chapters.title: Independence and civil war
text: Angola became independent in 1975, but the MPLA and UNITA fought a civil war drawing in the Soviet Union, Cuba, the US and South Africa. It ended in 2002 after UNITA's leader was killed.

keyTerms.meaning: The former rebel movement, now the main opposition.
